rationale: The run produced log/import_stats_final.log (via do/import_stats_final.do), which summarizes trade levels in BN 2007 US$. US imports from China (l_totimp_usch): 1991=26.27168, 2000=121.5563, 2007=330.0224 -> matches paper 26.3/121.6/330.0 exactly; derived growth (330.0224/26.27168-1)*100 = 1156.2% matches the paper's 1156%. US exports to China (l_totexp_usch): 1992=10.32224, 2000=23.00427, 2007=57.41103 -> matches paper 10.3/23.0/57.4; derived growth = 456.2% matches 456%. China's share of US low-income imports (China / (China + other low-income col.3, l_totimp_uslw), which the xls notes confirm excludes China): 1991 = 26.27168/(26.27168+7.686292) = 77.37% (matches paper 77.4% exactly), 2007 = 330.0224/(330.0224+45.43324) = 87.90% vs paper 89.8% — a 2.1% relative error, within the 5% cell tolerance. The parallel 'other high-income' cross-check (otch/(otch+otlw)) gives 75.3% -> 89.4% vs the paper's stated 75.4% -> 89.5%, confirming the share construction. All cells fall within 5% relative error, so the table matches.
